historical_references.reference: Subhash Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist who sought to free India from British rule during World War II. He formed the Indian National Army (INA) and led it in an unsuccessful attempt to invade India from Japanese-held territories in Southeast Asia. Bose is considered a hero by many Indians for his efforts to gain independence.

historical_references.reference: Subhash Mukherjee, also known as Subhas Chandra Bose, was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was twice elected President of the Indian National Congress and led the Swadeshi movement, which advocated for the Boycott of British goods and the use of Indian-made products. Bose was arrested several times by the British for his political activities and was exiled to Europe, where he eventually formed the Indian National Army.
